name: Benign Keratosis (Seborrheic Keratosis)
description: Benign keratosis (often seborrheic keratosis) is a very common non-cancerous skin growth. It often appears as a waxy, brown, black, or tan raised spot that looks 'stuck on' the skin. They are harmless and never turn into skin cancer.
common_symptoms: Round or oval raised spot that looks like melted candle wax dropped on the skin
Slightly raised, rough, or wart-like texture
Color ranges from light tan to dark brown or black
May occasionally itch or catch on clothing
Appears commonly on the chest, back, neck, or face
causes: Natural skin aging and genetic factors
Exact cause is unknown, but they are not caused by viral infections or sun damage alone
risk_factors: Age over 50 years (they become more common as people get older)
first_aid: Leave the spot alone if it is not irritated
If irritated by clothing, cover loosely with a bandage
Do not scratch, pinch, or try to peel off the growth
precautions: Avoid scratching or picking at the lesions
Keep watch for any sudden change in color or irregular borders to rule out other conditions
Wear loose, soft clothing if spots rub against seams or waistbands
home_care: Gently wash the area with regular soap and water
Moisturize skin if dry or mildly itchy
Never attempt home surgery or acid removal
do_not: DO NOT attempt to scrape, burn, or cut off the growths yourself
DO NOT use unprescribed wart removers or salicylic acid patches
DO NOT assume every dark spot is harmless without checking if it rapidly changes
red_flags: Rapid development of dozens of new spots over weeks
Spontaneous bleeding, ulceration, or oozing without injury
The spot becomes asymmetrical with jagged edges and multiple colors
when_to_see_doctor: See a doctor or dermatologist if a spot bleeds, becomes painful, or if you are not certain whether it is a harmless growth or something more serious.
prevention: No proven way to prevent benign keratoses as they are related to age and genetics
Maintain healthy skin care and routine skin self-checks
